objective: Integrate the audit chain into the existing EventAPI in app/events.py: post_event reads the buffer's current newest item, computes prev_entry_hash (GENESIS for the first item) and entry_hash via app/audit.py per C1, and appends {id, **payload, prev_entry_hash, entry_hash} to the RingBuffer; add GET /events?audit=true per C3 returning {'audit_chain': [{event_id, prev_entry_hash, entry_hash}, ...]} in storage order ([] when empty); strip prev_entry_hash/entry_hash at the API boundary so every C2 response (POST /events, GET /events?since=) stays byte-exact in shape; observable outcome: tests/test_audit.py passes (audit query shape + no audit-field leak in C2) and the pre-existing tests/test_events.py stays green unmodified.

files: app/audit.py (new — T01's module, consumed via the C1 interface)
concepts: RingBuffer.read_all() ordering: oldest surviving item first; buffer wraps at capacity (oldest overwritten)
frozen-response discipline: audit fields are stored in the buffer but stripped at the API boundary — C2 shapes are byte-exact invariants
chain append = read newest item (if any) -> prev = GENESIS or that item's entry_hash -> hash per C1 -> append extended item

inputs: contracts C1/C2/C3 (full specs inlined in frozen_contracts)

frozen_contracts.spec: Audit entry data stored inside each event item in the RingBuffer: the stored item is {id: 'e<n>', <event payload fields>, prev_entry_hash: str, entry_hash: str} where prev_entry_hash = entry_hash of the previously appended item (or GENESIS = sha256(b'genesis').hexdigest() for the first item ever appended) and entry_hash = sha256(canonical_json({id, prev_entry_hash})).hexdigest() with canonical_json = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')). Chain order = RingBuffer storage order (oldest surviving first). The API layer never exposes prev_entry_hash/entry_hash outside the C3 query.

FROZEN, unchanged: POST /events -> 201 {'id': 'e<n>'}; GET /events?since=<id> -> 200 {'events': [...]} where each item has EXACTLY the keys the client posted plus 'id' (audit fields stripped at the API boundary — no prev_entry_hash/entry_hash in the response); unknown since id -> 404 {'error': 'unknown since id: <id>'}. Existing tests in tests/test_events.py stay green against this contract.

New: GET /events?audit=true -> 200 {'audit_chain': [{'event_id': str, 'prev_entry_hash': str, 'entry_hash': str}, ...]} in storage order (oldest surviving first); empty buffer -> 200 {'audit_chain': []}. This is the only API surface that exposes audit fields.

allowed_dependencies.what: app/audit.py — C1-conformant hash functions and verify(); consume by import, never modify

non_goals: No changes to app/storage.py (platform-frozen: exactly one 1024-slot overwriting ring, no second store, no change this release cycle)
No changes to app/audit.py (T01-owned; suspected defects go to T03's owns_fixes_for route)
No changes or weakening of tests/test_events.py — it must remain green exactly as written
No external reporting/export, no file persistence, no hashing performance work
implementation_constraints: Append path: items = store.read_all(); newest = items[-1] if items else None; prev = GENESIS if newest is None else newest['entry_hash']; extended item = {'id': eid, **payload, 'prev_entry_hash': prev, 'entry_hash': hash per C1}; store.append(extended item) — event retention stays 1024 (no parallel stream)

Strip audit fields at the API boundary in every C2 response: POST /events returns exactly (201, {'id': eid}); each item in GET /events?since= output is the payload keys + 'id' only — 'prev_entry_hash'/'entry_hash' must never appear
GET /events?audit=true: 200 {'audit_chain': [{event_id, prev_entry_hash, entry_hash}, ...]} in storage order; {'audit_chain': []} when empty

The audit parameter is meaningful only on the read path (C3 is the only surface exposing audit fields): POST /events behavior is unchanged whether or not the audit parameter is present — the frozen 201 {'id': eid}; do not invent a new error response for that case
keep EventAPI's existing call compatibility: post_event(payload) and list_events(since) behave exactly as before for existing callers
pure stdlib; no new dependencies; touch no files outside owned_paths

deliverables.what: EventAPI with chain append in post_event, audit=true query handler, and C2 response stripping
API-level tests: audit query shape, no audit-field leak in C2 responses

acceptance_tests.description: After two posts, GET /events?audit=true returns {'audit_chain': [2 entries in storage order]} whose fields match the stored items, and verify() over those items returns status 'ok'
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_audit.test_audit_query_shape -v → 1 test passes, exit code 0

acceptance_tests.description: After posts, every item in GET /events?since= responses has exactly the posted keys + 'id' — 'prev_entry_hash' and 'entry_hash' are absent (C2 byte-exact); GET /events?since=unknown-id returns 404 {'error': 'unknown since id: unknown-id'} unchanged
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_audit.test_no_audit_leak_in_c2 -v → 1 test passes, exit code 0

failure_cases.expected_behavior: the first appended item stores prev_entry_hash = GENESIS, so verify() returns head anchored=true

failure_cases.scenario: POST /events with the audit parameter present
failure_cases.expected_behavior: the POST returns 201 {'id': eid} unchanged — audit is read-only per C3; the contracts define no error shape for this case and none is invented
